items.title: Avakian George — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Dick Broderick, who was an associate of mine when I was with RCA in 1960, ’62

ctx.x: Barney? Oh Barney, yes, Barney Josephson. He only came to a couple of them, because, as he put it, “This is a lot of fun, but I live it every day. I can’t stand more.” The third year was done at a classroom building at the east end of – at the NYU campus, on one of the upper floors. At that point, Marshall Stearns had settled into New York. I talked to him about expanding this, because I said, “Look, this is fun, to give informal talks, but I can’t really get into it too deeply, and I think the university wants…

That grew into a regular NARAS course at NYU. Finally, Dick Broderick, who was an associate of mine when I was with RCA in 1960, ’62, left RCA and joined the NYU faculty and ran a course within the music department which included engineering and so forth. My son took it and became a rather good engineer and did – what do they call it? Not apprentice work, but – what’s the word? It’s like a . . .
